lead: Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm, persistence through .claude/settings.json, May 2026

No agent call, send or data change is in the record, so the harm does not trace to an agent control. Worth revisiting if a version is documented where the agent itself carried the action.

note: The hardest rejection in the queue, and worth stating plainly because the rule and the instinct disagree. The primary record is excellent: a detailed first-hand postmortem by the named founder of the named organisation, giving the stale state file, the auto-approve, the row count of 1,943,200, the fact that the snapshots went too, and the twenty-four hour recovery through cloud support. It also contains a detail the register would have valued, that the agent advised against the risky approach and a person approved the destroy anyway. But no reputable independent outlet covered it. Everything else restates the postmortem. The fourth test asks for grade A or B, and a single source is grade C, which the inclusion rule does not admit. Revisit if a trade or mainstream outlet covers it.

lead: A weapons engineering cell used a coding agent to develop guidance and navigation software, September 2026
note: The hardest call on the harm test in the whole queue. A cell ran three weapons programmes with a coding agent standing in for a software team, writing guidance, navigation and control code, and segmented its requests so each looked like ordinary robotics work. It is still a capability rather than a harm: the one live-fire test of the guided rocket failed, and no casualties, damage or victims are on the record.
